transpose.heading: What CSV transpose does
transpose.text: CSV transpose turns a row-oriented table into a column-oriented layout, or the reverse, by swapping rows and columns. The first row of your upload is treated as data like every other row, not as a special header that is dropped or kept fixed on the side. After transpose, what was row one becomes column one, row two becomes column two, and so on. If some rows in the original file are shorter than the widest row, the parser pads them with blank cells before rotating so every position is defined. The tool runs entirely in your browser: your file is not uploaded to a server for conversion. You pick a delimiter, run transpose, skim a preview of the first twelve rows of the result, then download the full transposed CSV with every row included. Input is expected to be UTF-8 text with a single header row only in the sense that you may have one; it is still rotated like any other line. Input delimiter choice affects how fields are split on read; comma, semicolon, tab, pipe and automatic detection are supported. Output uses commas. This page accepts CSV only, not Excel workbooks; use the Excel to CSV tool first if your data is in .xlsx or .xls format.

transpose.heading: When transpose is useful
transpose.text: People use transpose when a report was exported with dates or categories across the top but analysis tools want one row per observation, or when a sensor log stores channels as rows and you need time in the first column instead. It is also handy for reshaping small matrices for charts, joining to another file that shares an ID in the first column, or comparing the same entities listed vertically in one file and horizontally in another. Because the operation is a straight geometric swap with blank padding, it does not interpret types: numbers and dates stay as the text that appeared in each cell. Transpose does not deduplicate columns, merge files, or fix header naming; it only reorients the grid you provide. If you need to combine several CSV exports into one long table, use the CSV merge tool after you have aligned headers manually or ensured each file uses the same header spelling. If you need live formula results from Excel rather than last-saved displayed values, re-save or calculate in Excel before export, because this tool never opens workbooks.

transpose.heading: Step-by-step workflow
transpose.text: Start by preparing a UTF-8 CSV within the size and shape limits: up to ten megabytes per file, up to one hundred thousand data rows and one thousand columns in the source grid, with transposed output allowed up to two thousand columns. Open the transpose page, choose the delimiter that matches your file, and upload the CSV. Click transpose to parse all rows including the first line, pad short rows to the width of the longest row, build the rotated matrix, and render the preview limited to the first twelve result rows so the page stays responsive. Open the preview table to confirm that output row one matches the first input column read top to bottom, that quoting around commas or semicolons survived correctly, and that trailing empty fields did not collapse in a misleading way. When the layout looks right, download the CSV to get the complete transposed dataset with no row cap on export. Keep your original file unchanged as a backup. For wide inputs, remember the output row count equals the original column count; very wide files can become tall exports that are still valid CSV but heavy in spreadsheet apps.

transpose.heading: How padding and rotation work
transpose.text: The implementation reads the file as delimited text, splits each line into fields using your selected delimiter with standard CSV quoting rules, and determines the maximum field count across all rows. Any row with fewer fields gets empty strings appended on the right until its length matches that maximum. Then for each original column index, the tool collects the value at that index from row zero, row one, row two, through the last row, and writes that collection as one new row in the output. The first input row becomes the first column of the output, while the first input column becomes the first output row. Blank pads matter when, for example, row five had only three fields but row one had six: positions four through six for row five are treated as empty before the swap, so the transposed columns that came from those positions still exist and show blanks where data was missing. Completely blank input records are skipped; otherwise the tool retains fields and it does not trim spaces inside fields unless your source already had trimmed values.

transpose.heading: Concrete input and output example
transpose.text: Suppose you upload a comma-separated file with three rows and four columns, with no irregular widths. Row one is: alpha, beta, gamma, delta. Row two is: 1, 2, 3, 4. Row three is: x, y, z, w. After transpose with comma delimiter, you should see four rows. Row one becomes: alpha, 1, x. Row two becomes: beta, 2, y. Row three becomes: gamma, 3, z. Row four becomes: delta, 4, w. Notice how the first output row is the first column of the input read from top to bottom, not a copy of the old header row pinned separately. If the second input row were shorter, say only alpha, 1 with two fields while other rows still had four, padding would add two blank fields on that row before rotation, and the third and fourth output rows would include empty cells in the slot that came from those padded positions. Quoted fields containing commas stay single cells on both read and write; the downloaded file uses quoting when needed for a comma delimiter.

transpose.heading: Checking results and delimiter choices
transpose.text: Always compare dimensions: output row count should equal the original column count after padding, and output column count should equal the original row count. Spot-check several cells by tracing back to the source coordinates: output at row i column j should equal input at row j column i when both use zero-based indexing on the padded grid. If every line in the preview looks like one giant field, the delimiter is probably wrong for your file, or the file uses a different encoding than UTF-8, which can produce parse errors or odd characters. If transpose fails immediately, read the error message: it may cite file size, row or column limits, parse failures, or encoding problems. The preview is only twelve rows; long files require scrolling in a local editor after download to verify the tail. Empty trailing delimiters at line ends create empty fields that participate in transpose the same as explicit values. Tabs and semicolons are common in European exports; pick the delimiter that matches the file rather than forcing comma. The default setting attempts to detect the input delimiter automatically.

transpose.heading: Limits, failures, and related tasks
transpose.text: Hard limits are enforced before and during processing: ten megabytes maximum per file, one hundred thousand data rows and one thousand columns on input, and up to two thousand columns in the transposed output shape. Exceeding any limit returns a clear error and no download. Malformed quoting and unrecoverable parse errors stop the run with a message. Invalid UTF-8 can appear as replacement characters, so check the source and preview. Because work happens in the browser, extremely large grids may stress memory or tab performance even when within published caps. Transpose does not support .xlsx or .xls on this page; convert with the Excel to CSV tool, download UTF-8 CSV, then transpose here. To stack multiple CSV files by headers, use merge, not transpose. Merge requires consistent header rows and row widths across files; transpose leaves you with a single file in a new orientation. Neither transpose nor merge recalculates Excel formulas. For Excel sources, exported cached displayed values are what subsequent CSV tools see. If transpose is unsuitable because you only wanted to turn the first row into headers without rotating IDs, you need a different operation than full matrix transpose; this tool always rotates the entire rectangle including row one.

merge.heading: What CSV merge does
merge.text: CSV merge combines multiple CSV files into one table by vertically appending data rows. All files must present a header row as their first line. The merge key is the exact text of each header cell, case-sensitive and including spaces: Name and name are two different columns. The tool builds the union of all header names seen across files, orders those columns in the order they first appear when scanning files in the sequence you selected, and writes one output header row using that unified list. Each file's data rows are mapped into that union: where a file has a column for a given header, values copy across; where a file lacks that header, blank cells are inserted. Duplicate header names within a single file are rejected, as are blank header cells or any data row whose field count does not match that file's header width. Files are read in the browser only; nothing is sent to a server. The preview shows the first twelve merged rows; the downloaded CSV contains all merged rows. Input CSV should be UTF-8. This page does not read Excel; convert workbooks separately first.

merge.heading: When merge fits your task
merge.text: Merge suits combining monthly exports that share the same schema, appending new batches from a form export, or stitching regional files where some regions omit optional columns that should still appear in the combined file. It is the right tool when you want one long dataset with aligned columns, not when you want to join two tables on a key with different numbers of rows or aggregate duplicates. Merge preserves row order within each file and processes files in the order reported by the file picker, so earlier files' rows appear before later files' rows in the output. It does not sort, filter, deduplicate, or validate business rules. If two files use different spellings for the same concept, such as SKU versus sku, both columns appear in the union and you must fix headers before merge or clean the result afterward. Transpose is unrelated: it rotates one file. Merge never swaps rows and columns. If your problem is Excel worksheet content with formulas, export to CSV using displayed values first; merge only sees the text CSV representation.

merge.heading: Step-by-step workflow
merge.text: Prepare each CSV at or under ten megabytes, within one hundred thousand data rows and one thousand columns per file, encoded as UTF-8. Confirm the first line of every file is the header row and that every subsequent line has exactly as many fields as that header, including empty fields represented by consecutive delimiters or trailing delimiters as needed. Confirm header cells are non-empty and unique within each file. On the merge page, choose the delimiter, select at least two files together and check the resulting row order, and run merge. The tool parses each file, validates headers and row widths, accumulates the union header list, appends mapped rows, then shows a twelve-row preview. Inspect header order and a few mapped rows, especially for files that lacked optional columns, to see blanks where you expect gaps. Download when satisfied to obtain the full merged CSV. If any file fails validation, the operation should report which problem occurred rather than producing a partial merge with misaligned columns.

merge.heading: Union headers, duplicates, and column order
merge.text: Header union logic uses exact string equality on header names from the first row, with case sensitivity. The output column order follows first occurrence across the ordered file list: if file one has headers id, name and file two adds age, the merged header becomes id, name, age because age first appeared in file two after file one's headers were registered. If file two instead had name, id, age, the union order is still id, name from file one first, then age; file two's row values are placed under the correct union columns regardless of that file's local column order. Two headers that look alike but differ by case occupy two output columns. The tool does not rename, fuzzy-match, or collapse synonyms. Duplicate header names on the same first row are an error because the mapper would not know which physical column to read. Blank header titles are an error for the same reason. The merge does not preserve multiple header rows; only row one is structural, and all following lines are data.

merge.heading: Concrete merge example
merge.text: File A, comma-delimited: first line id,name; second line 1,Ada; third line 2,Bob. File B: first line id,age; second line 3,30; third line 4,25. Union headers in processing order are id, name, age. Output header row: id,name,age. Output data rows: 1,Ada, with a blank third field; 2,Bob, blank third field; 3, blank name field, 30; 4, blank name, 25. File B rows gained an empty name column because name existed only in file A. File A rows gained an empty age column. If file B had mistakenly used Id instead of id, the union would treat Id as a separate column and file B's identifiers would land under Id while file A's stayed under id, which is usually unwanted and should be fixed by editing headers before merge. If a data row in file B had three fields but its header had two, merge rejects the file for inconsistent row width rather than silently dropping or merging fields.

merge.heading: Validation errors and how to fix them
merge.text: Common failures include duplicate header names within one file, empty header cells, data rows with fewer or more delimited fields than the header count, files over ten megabytes, or grids exceeding row or column limits. Fix duplicate or blank headers in a text editor or spreadsheet by exporting CSV again with a clean single header row. Fix width mismatches by ensuring every data line has the same number of separators as expected; embedded line breaks inside quoted fields are fine, but unquoted stray commas create extra fields. Align delimiters with the selector on the page. If only some files use semicolon, normalize them before merge or merge in batches after conversion. Encoding issues often show as replacement characters or parse errors; re-save source as UTF-8. The preview helps catch logical mistakes such as two id columns after merge; those are data hygiene issues, not tool bugs. Remember merge does not check that id values are unique across files.

merge.heading: Limits and how merge differs from transpose and Excel export
merge.text: Each input file shares the same caps: ten megabytes, one hundred thousand rows, one thousand columns, UTF-8 CSV. The merged output is capped at 100,000 data rows, 1,000 columns and five million cells; each run accepts up to 20 files. Merge appends rows; transpose rotates one file. Excel to CSV extracts one worksheet's displayed cell values to UTF-8 CSV without recalculating formulas or keeping colors, fonts, or number formats; that CSV can then be merged with others if headers validate. There is no Excel import on the merge page itself. Downloaded merge output uses comma delimiters with quoting as needed and includes every merged data row, not only the twelve-row preview. Failed validation on any single file should abort the merge with a descriptive error so you do not download a table built from an incomplete set. For related preparation tasks, standardize header spelling across exports, remove extra title lines above headers, and verify row counts in a terminal or editor before combining sensitive datasets.

excel.heading: What Excel to CSV conversion does
excel.text: This tool converts a single worksheet from an Excel .xlsx or .xls workbook into one UTF-8 CSV file. After upload, you select which sheet to export when the workbook contains more than one. Conversion reads the stored cell values that Excel last cached for display: what you would typically see in the cell after opening the file, not live re-evaluation of formulas against a full calculation engine in the browser. Numeric dates, formatted numbers, and text become plain text fields in CSV form. Formatting such as fill colors, fonts, borders, column widths, merged cell presentation, and conditional formatting rules are not carried over. Each run exports exactly one worksheet; other sheets remain in the workbook untouched until you convert them in separate passes. Processing is local to your browser without uploading the workbook to a conversion server. The UI shows a preview of the first twelve rows of the CSV text; the download contains all rows that were read from the used range of that sheet, subject to the same row and column limits as other tools on the site.

excel.heading: When to use this instead of Save As in Excel
excel.text: Use in-browser conversion when you do not have Excel installed, you want a quick one-sheet UTF-8 CSV on another operating system, or you prefer not to email a workbook through unrelated desktop steps. It is appropriate when cached values in the file are trustworthy: you opened and saved the sheet in Excel recently, values are constants, or you accept that formula cells export whatever was last calculated and stored. It is not appropriate when you must guarantee fresh formula results after macro or external data changes without opening Excel, or when you need multiple sheets in one CSV file, because this tool never merges sheets. For CSV-only utilities such as transpose or merge, run Excel to CSV first, then upload the resulting CSV to those pages; they do not accept .xlsx directly. If your workflow needs formatting, pivot tables, or charts, keep the workbook format; CSV is for data interchange, not presentation.

excel.heading: Step-by-step workflow
excel.text: Confirm the workbook is at most ten megabytes and that the target sheet's used area fits within one hundred thousand data rows and one thousand columns. Choose the .xlsx or .xls file and click Convert. The first sheet is displayed; choose another worksheet and click Convert again to export it. The reader walks the sheet's populated range, resolves displayed values for each cell, serializes rows using comma separators, and fills the preview with the first twelve lines of the CSV string. Scan the preview for sensible column splits, empty leading rows if the sheet had blank top margin, and formula cells that show zero or old dates suggesting stale cache. Download the CSV for the full export. Open in a text editor or import into your next tool with UTF-8 encoding specified. To convert another sheet, repeat with the same or a new upload; there is no batch all-sheets zip from this page. Save the CSV under a clear name indicating sheet name and export date if you manage many extracts.

excel.heading: Displayed values, formulas, and dates
excel.text: Excel files often store both a formula expression and a cached result. This exporter uses the cached result path appropriate to the file format so cells appear as users last saw them in Excel, without invoking a full recalculation pipeline in JavaScript. That means an IF or VLOOKUP cell exports the last saved outcome, which might differ from what Excel would show after refreshing external links today. Constant cells export their literals directly. Date cells typically export as the displayed serial formatting Excel cached, which may look like a calendar string or a number depending on how the workbook was saved; downstream tools may need explicit date parsing. Empty cells produce empty fields. Cells with errors cached as error displays may export error text visible in the sheet. There is no option here to export formula strings instead of values. If you need formula text, copy from Excel's formula bar or use a specialized Excel feature. Boolean values become whatever string representation the reader obtains from the cell record.

excel.heading: Concrete conversion example
excel.text: Imagine a small .xlsx sheet named Sales with cells A1:C2 where A1 is Item, B1 is Qty, C1 is Price, A2 is Apple, B2 is 10, C2 contains a formula multiplying quantity by a unit price with cached displayed value 45.50, formatted as currency in Excel but stored as display text 45.50 or a localized variant depending on cache. The CSV header row becomes three fields: Item, Qty, Price. The second row contains Apple, 10, and the displayed cached result, which may include currency symbols from the cell format. A blank row 3 outside the used range does not appear. If row 2 instead held a formula with no cached value in a damaged file, you might see an empty field or an odd token; repairing in Excel and re-saving fixes cache. The downloaded CSV uses commas between fields and quotes values containing commas.

excel.heading: Worksheet selection and range behavior
excel.text: Multi-sheet workbooks require you to choose one worksheet per conversion. Hidden or very hidden sheets may still appear in the list if the reader enumerates them; sheets exceeding the row or column guards are rejected. Leading entirely blank rows and columns at the edge of the used range may still affect how many blank fields appear at the start of a row if the format stores a rectangular used range including blanks. After export, verify column alignment in the preview because merged cells in Excel can confuse rectangular reads: you may see values only in the top-left cell of a merged block with blanks in sibling columns that visually spanned in Excel. Charts, images, and shapes are skipped. Tables defined as Excel tables still export as cell values in the grid. For .xls legacy binaries, support covers the same conceptual behavior though very old files might fail parsing with an error message. One worksheet at a time is a deliberate scope limit, not a multi-select omission you can toggle on.

excel.heading: Limits, failures, and chaining to CSV tools
excel.text: Files above ten megabytes fail early. Sheets with more than one hundred thousand rows or one thousand columns hit limits during read or write. Corrupt archives, password-protected workbooks without provided passwords, or unsupported encryption typically produce errors instead of partial CSV. Browser memory may struggle below theoretical limits on low-end devices. Output is UTF-8 CSV with comma delimiter and RFC-style quoting when fields contain separators or line breaks. After download, transpose can rotate the CSV including its first row as data; merge can append multiple CSV exports if each has valid headers and consistent row widths. Neither chained tool reads Excel natively. If merge reports duplicate headers, fix the CSV header line in an editor. If transpose widens beyond two thousand columns, reduce source rows or split the sheet before conversion. Recalculate important formulas in Excel before export when stale cache would cause wrong downstream analysis.
